Using \(A = \frac12 bc \sin 60^\circ = 10\sqrt3\),

\[
\frac12 bc \cdot \frac{\sqrt3}{2}=10\sqrt3 \implies bc=40.
\]

Since \(a+b+c=20\), we have \(b+c=20-a\).

By the Law of Cosines at \(A=60^\circ\),

\[
a^2=b^2+c^2-bc=(b+c)^2-3bc.
\]

So

\[
a^2=(20-a)^2-3(40).
\]

\[
a^2=(20-a)^2-120
\]

\[
a^2=400-40a+a^2-120
\]

\[
40a=280 \implies a=7.
\]

\[
\boxed{7}
\]
